title: Repeat Purchase Rate Calculation
description: Calculate the **repeat purchase rate**: the percentage of customers who have placed **more than one order**. Return a single row with the rate rounded to 2 decimal places.
solution_sql: SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(CASE WHEN order_count > 1 THEN 1 END) / COUNT(*), 2) AS repeat_rate_pct FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS order_count FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) customer_counts

test_cases.description: 8 customers total. Repeat buyers (>1 order): C1(2), C2(3), C3(2), C4(2) = 4. One-time buyers: C5,C6,C7,C8. Rate = 4/8 = 50.00%

hints: Use a subquery to count orders per customer, then in the outer query use CASE WHEN order_count > 1 THEN 1 END inside COUNT() to count only repeat buyers.
Divide the repeat buyer count by the total customer count and multiply by 100 — both can come from the same outer query against the subquery.
explanation: The subquery computes per-customer order counts. The outer query evaluates these counts: COUNT(CASE WHEN order_count > 1 THEN 1 END) returns 4 (customers 1, 2, 3, 4 have 2+, 3, 2, 2 orders respectively); COUNT(*) = 8 (all customers). Repeat rate = 4/8 × 100 = 50.00%. This metric is fundamental for e-commerce retention analysis.
